category_title: Preschoolers at risk for developmental delays with mild to moderate language disorders
minimal_context: The student and a peer are in the classroom with kitchen toys, tasked with developing a play plan for the session.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time to make a play plan for the kitchen toys. What do you want to do with them?

STUDENT: (Stands away from the peer and looks at the floor, appearing lonely and anxious instead of initiating a conversation.)

TUTOR: Talk to your friend and decide what to play.

STUDENT: (Remains completely silent, making no comments to the peer about the toys.)

TUTOR: Come on, you need to make a plan together. Tell each other what to do.

STUDENT: (Shows increased anxiety during the awkward silence and begins to have a temper tantrum, throwing a plastic plate and refusing to follow directions.)

options.A: Provide warnings of upcoming transitions before moving on to the play plan activity with the kitchen toys during the session.
options.B: Allow the student to keep the plastic plate under the condition that they do not throw it at their peer, and break off the play session.
options.C: Suggest roles for the children (e.g., 'You can cook and your friend can set the table'), and role-play and model ways to use the kitchen toys and talk to each other.
options.D: Provide visual expectations or rules for the play plan activity, along with a visual chart with the time on it.
